# B2B2C Support

`customer_support.model.b2b2c` · model · parent `—`

> We supply a partner, the partner serves consumers, and support has to serve both. The structural fact that makes this its own model and not a blend of the other two: there are two customers with genuinely conflicting interests, and only one of them has a contract with us. The partner owns the end-user relationship and does not want us in it; the end user owns the pain and does not care about our contracting chain. Entitlement is inherited rather than held — an end user has no plan of their own, only whatever their partner bought — so entitlement verification requires resolving identity upward through the partner before anything can be promised. During an incident this inverts: the partner's support team becomes a queue of its own, contacting us on behalf of thousands, and their tickets are all the same ticket. Two habits break here in opposite directions. A B2C operator answers the end user directly because it is faster, and in doing so destroys the partner's ability to run their own support and their record of it. A B2B operator refuses to speak to anyone but the partner, which is correct on a Tuesday and indefensible during an outage the partner cannot explain.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| requester | either the partner's own support or operations team, or the partner's end customer — and frequently we cannot tell which from the ticket alone |
| typical_resolution_hours | 12 |
| volume_shape | low steady volume from a handful of partner teams, punctuated by correlated mass volume when a partner has an incident and its consumers overflow to us |
| staffing_model | partner-facing pooled team with named contacts per partner, plus an escalation path that can reach engineering fast |
| coverage | aligned to the partner's own coverage commitments, which are usually wider than ours |
| automation_level | moderate for partner teams, who are technical and repeat contacts; near zero for end users, who arrive confused about who we even are |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.requester`

Requires `role`


> Partner-agent or end-user is the single most consequential property in this branch. Everything downstream — tone, entitlement, what may be disclosed, whether we reply at all — resolves off it, and the canonical object treats it as descriptive.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.entitlement`

Requires `plan`


> Inherited entitlement. The end user's rights are a projection of the partner's contract, so the entitlement object must resolve through a party who is not in the conversation. An unresolved chain means nothing may be promised, not that the default applies.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.incident`


> An incident here has two comms audiences on different clocks: the partner needs engineering-grade detail immediately so they can hold their own line, and the end users need reassurance they will mostly receive from the partner, not from us.
